newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Hillary Clinton begins vist to Amsterdam.
newsitem.headline: Hillary Clinton begins vist to Amsterdam.

text.p: U.S. First Lady Hillary Rodham Clinton began a day's programme of visits in the Dutch capital on Tuesday, landing at Schiphol airport ahead of President Bill Clinton, expected in Amsterdam later on Tuesday.
Clinton is due to fly to Schiphol from Paris on Tuesday evening in readiness for a bi-annual meeting on Wednesday with the European Union presidency, currently held by the Dutch.

Mrs Clinton was met by Rita Kok, wife of Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok at Schiphol, and a small Dutch military honour guard before leaving for Amsterdam and an engagement at the University of Amsterdam where she is scheduled to give a speech on issues concerning, democracy, children's welfare and women.

A spokeswoman for the University said Rodham Clinton would address an audience of 600 people, mainly women drawn from the educational, care and cultural sectors and several Dutch women members of parliament. Some 100 were guests of the university, while the remainder had been invited by the U.S. Embassy.
A spokeswoman for the City of Amsterdam said Mayor Schelto Patijn, struggling with illness, would briefly greet Mrs Clinton privately on arrival.
Her programme includes a boat cruise through Amsterdam followed by a visit to the Rijksmuseum, the Netherlands' national museum and art gallery.

Mrs Clinton rounds off her Amsterdam programme with a visit to the canalside home of Anne Frank, the young Jewish girl whose diaries tell how she hid from Nazi occupiers during World War Two before her capture and imprisonment in Auschwitz.
The First Lady then departs for the Hague to meet the President who will arrive by helicopter from Amsterdam's Schiphol airport ahead of his EU programme on Wednesday.

Clinton's visit is combined with a commemoration of the 50th anniversary of the postwar Marshall Aid Plan which will be attended by leaders from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, which groups the countries of Europe with Canada and the United States.
